A massive tiled mosaic of a ten-head hydra in the throes of casting some grand, unimaginable spell covers the entire far wall and ceiling of the room. Slender tentacles have crept into the temple of Cassien, unafraid of the tyrant god's wrath, and twined around pillars that were once beautiful. [Dremsyl's Tower, Shrine to Cassien]
Slender tentacles have crept into the temple of Cassien, unafraid of the tyrant god's wrath, and twined around pillars that were once beautiful. Now most of the obsidian and ruby inlaid columns have fallen to the ground, shattered by the crushing strength of the muscled appendages of the tower beast. A faded mural of a stalking panther covers the back wall, the intricate detail in the painting, suggests it was created by a true master of the craft in loving devotion of his vain god. An obsidian altar sits before the masterpiece, an exquisite carving of a goshawk, its wings outstretched once sat upon the volcanic stone, now it has fallen to the floor, one wing snapped off. No doubt the god Cassien has long since abandoned this place, but it still reeks of his power, and the tentacles of the fleshy monster feast off the residual magical energy of the shrine.

A faded mural of a stalking panther covers the back wall, the intricate detail in the painting, suggests it was created by a true master of the craft in loving devotion of his vain god. An obsidian altar sits before the masterpiece, an exquisite carving of a goshawk, its wings outstretched once sat upon the volcanic stone, now it has fallen to the floor, one wing snapped off. No doubt the god Cassien has long since abandoned this place, but it still reeks of his power, and the tentacles of the fleshy monster feast off the residual magical energy of the shrine.

The area is illuminated.

[Dremsyl's Tower, Dining Room]
The remnants of a beautifully wrought iron chandelier hang from the roof, just above a decayed wooden table. The room is smaller than the main dining room, perhaps the personal dining area of the master of the tower. The tapestries that still hang on the walls reveal in faded color that they were once masterpieces. A sodden piece of cloth covers the floor beneath the rotten wood table, it appears to be the hide of some great furred beast, but the water has damaged it beyond recognition. Because of the awkward tilting of the tower, much of the water streaming through the rest of the first floor has made its way here. Years of corrosive water has finally worn away the thick stone wall and the water has at last found a way out of the tower via dozens of holes where large stones once were. The water cascades out the holes in a constant stream into a cavern so dark no amount of light seems able to penetrate it.

The area is illuminated.

The grey flesh of the brain pulses with stolen magical energies and a shimmering rainbow of lights surround the brain matter in an entrancing aura. Glaring, blood-shot eyes stare out across the room, watching for any creature dim-witted enough to walk right into the heart of the hostile beast. The smell of rotting meat has become overpowering as the creature throbs with boundless rage and its massive limbs thrash with abandon. A screeching hum fills the room from an unidentifiable source, as the monster seems to have no true mouth with which to speak.

The area is illuminated.

[Dremsyl's Tower, Shrine to Karishta]
A massive tiled mosaic of a ten-head hydra in the throes of casting some grand, unimaginable spell covers the entire far wall and ceiling of the room. [Dremsyl's Tower, Shrine to Cassien]
Slender tentacles have crept into the temple of Cassien, unafraid of the tyrant god's wrath, and twined around pillars that were once beautiful. Now most of the obsidian and ruby inlaid columns have fallen to the ground, shattered by the crushing strength of the muscled appendages of the tower beast. A faded mural of a stalking panther covers the back wall, the intricate detail in the painting, suggests it was created by a true master of the craft in loving devotion of his vain god. An obsidian altar sits before the masterpiece, an exquisite carving of a goshawk, its wings outstretched once sat upon the volcanic stone, now it has fallen to the floor, one wing snapped off. No doubt the god Cassien has long since abandoned this place, but it still reeks of his power, and the tentacles of the fleshy monster feast off the residual magical energy of the shrine.

[Popper Street]
A shadowy back alley winds its way between the crumbling stone walls of two old storefronts. The abandoned stores have boards over their broken windows and pebbles litter the front porches. One of the roofs have begun to fall into the inside of the store, as wooden beams can be seen dangling down towards the floor through cracks in the wooden boards outside.

The area is illuminated.

Obvious exits are: west, east, dark, narrow alleyway

e
e

[Popper Street]
A broken wooden gate swings erratically on its hinges, banging against the old iron lock. Though there is a slight wind, it would not be enough to make the gate swing that hard. Passing the gate, denizens notice three small Zacotl children roughly swinging the gate to make the noise and entertain themselves without parental supervision.

The area is illuminated.

Obvious exits are: west, east

e

[Popper Street]
High-pitched dog growls can be heard from the back of a shady building. The rafters on the roof has fallen in, along with some of the wooden shingles. A young man smiles kindly as the soldiers pass the house by; he enters the house where a young woman can be seen holding a child and attempting to shush the canines. Old bones and scraps are strewn about the front yard beneath a clothes line.

The area is illuminated.

Obvious exits are: west, east

e

[Popper Street]
Near the main road, a well-dressed Silvarin gentleman sits at the side of Popper Street, nonchalantly reading the local newspaper for the latest issues and rumors. A group of children, diverse in their races, scuffle up to him and beg him for a mark. The Silvarin gives each child a crown and, left to himself and cheers of the children, he reads his paper. The soldiers pass him by quietly, moving on to the Southern Cross Road.

The area is illuminated.

Obvious exits are: west, east


[Southern Cross Road]
Neatly kept cobblestones lead north and south the cracks between them free of dirt and debris. The large black gate which allows entrance to the city from Travers towers above several trees to the south. To the north the road curves slightly then begins to straighten. The road both north and south is lined on either side by brass lanterns which hang close to the ground from dark walnut posts allowing for plenty of light even on the darkest nights. To the west and the east a neat but narrower road appears to parallel the tall city walls which dots the sky in the distance.

The area is illuminated.

Obvious exits are: west, south, east, north

n
n

[Southern Cross Road]
City guards pass by frequently as they make their rounds. To the west the roof of a large building can be seen peaking over a few trees. A small man made waterfall feeds a small pond which bubbles happily on the eastern edge of the road.

The area is illuminated.

Obvious exits are: south, north

n
n

[Southern Cross Road]
Oak trees and Birch trees which house several types of wildlife line the east and west side of the street.  A few small but functional benches are scattered neatly amongst the trees to allow for rest and relaxation. Hanging from a metal pole on the east side of the road is a small black sign with white lettering that reads "This road maintained by the Urda Merchants Council"

The area is illuminated.

Obvious exits are: south, north

n

[Urda Town Square Center]
The former site of a fierce battle for control of this great city was waged here, and on this site is where it's citizens celebrate that victory. Statues of the fallen heroes, and great leaders of the alliance adorn the tops of grand marble archways leading in all directions. They stand ever vigilant against any unseen enemy. The people of Urda flock here to barter and trade, to converse with friends, or just relax near the fountain and have a game of chess. Benches and tables dot the landscape near the edge of the fountain. Hawkers of all type roll through this area with their wares, hoping to make a few coins. Languages of all races are spoken here. The sheer din of the crowd reverberates throughout the area. Passersby stop to admire the detail of the arches as they enter and exit the city square.

The area is illuminated.

[Temple of the Eyranas]
Amazingly the interior of the temple is teaming with life. Birds fly freely amongst the tall trees and shrubs which give the appearance of the outside instead of in. Small animals scurry across the ground in an almost permanent state of play. A large fountain set in the center of the area spouts water high into the air which then settles back into the fountain without even the smallest splash. Statues of the Goddess's lie scattered among the various ponds and gardens of the temple. A small grassy pasture free of any growth takes its place on the northeastern side of the temple which sits beneath a beautiful green, moss covered altar. A gaggle of bushes trimmed to portray letters spells out the word "Life" in the northwestern corner of the temple. A small path that leads through some thick overgrowth to the west provides passage to another room. To the south an overgrown arch provides exit back to the street.

The area is illuminated.
